semantic_fragments.content: The USER INTERFACE SPECIFICATION shall consider: the USE SPECIFICATION (see 5.1); the known or foreseeable USE ERRORS associated with the MEDICAL DEVICE (see 5.2); and the HAZARD-RELATED USE SCENARIOS (see 5.4). The USER INTERFACE SPECIFICATION shall include: testable technical requirements relevant to the USER INTERFACE, including the requirements for those parts of the USER INTERFACE associated with the selected RISK CONTROL measures; an indication as to whether ACCOMPANYING DOCUMENTATION is required; and an indication as to whether MEDICAL DEVICE-specific training is required. The USER INTERFACE SPECIFICATION shall be stored in the USABILITY ENGINEERING FILE. The USER INTERFACE SPECIFICATION may be integrated into other specifications. See section 5.3 of Usability Engineering File (document no. CE-PT9L-12).

The MANUFACTURER shall establish and maintain a USER INTERFACE EVALUATION plan for the USER INTERFACE SPECIFICATION (section 5.7, 5.7.1). The USER INTERFACE EVALUATION plan shall: 1. document the objective and identify the method of any planned FORMATIVE EVALUATIONS and SUMMATIVE EVALUATIONS; 2. if USABILITY TESTS are employed, document which USER GROUPS are intended to be included in the test; document the test environment and other conditions of use, based on the USE SPECIFICATION; specify whether ACCOMPANYING DOCUMENTATION is provided during the test; and specify whether MEDICAL DEVICE-specific training is provided prior to the test and the minimum elapsed time between the training and the beginning of the test. USER INTERFACE EVALUATION methods may be quantitative or qualitative. USER INTERFACE EVALUATION may be performed in a variety of locations, such as in a laboratory setting, in a simulated USE ENVIRONMENT or in the actual USE ENVIRONMENT. The USER INTERFACE EVALUATION plan may be integrated into other plans. The USER INTERFACE EVALUATION plan shall be stored in the USABILITY ENGINEERING FILE. See section 7 of Usability Engineering File (document no. CE-PT9L-12).

FORMATIVE EVALUATION planning (5.7.2): The USER INTERFACE evaluation plan for FORMATIVE EVALUATION shall address: 1. the evaluation methods being used; 2. which part of the USER INTERFACE is being evaluated; and 3. when in the USABILITY ENGINEERING PROCESS to perform each of the USER INTERFACE EVALUATIONS. See section 7.1 of Usability Engineering File (document no. CE-PT9L-12).

SUMMATIVE EVALUATION planning (5.7.3): For each selected HAZARD-RELATED USE SCENARIO (see 5.5), the USER INTERFACE EVALUATION plan for SUMMATIVE EVALUATION shall specify: 1. the evaluation method being used and a rationale that the method produces OBJECTIVE EVIDENCE; 2. which part of the USER INTERFACE is being evaluated; 3. where applicable, the criteria for determining whether the information for SAFETY is perceivable, understandable and supports CORRECT USE of the MEDICAL DEVICE (4.1.3); 4. the availability of the ACCOMPANYING DOCUMENTATION and provision of training during the SUMMATIVE EVALUATION; and 5. for a USABILITY TEST: how the characteristics of the test participants are representative of the intended PROFILES; justifying how the test participants are grouped into distinct USER GROUPS for the purpose of determining the number of test participants; the test environment and conditions of use and a rationale for how they are adequately representative of the intended USE ENVIRONMENT; the definition of CORRECT USE for each HAZARD-RELATED USE SCENARIO; and the method of collecting data during the USABILITY TEST for the subsequent analysis of observed USE ERRORS and use difficulties. The SUMMATIVE EVALUATION may be performed in a single evaluation or multiple evaluations. See section 7.2 of Usability Engineering File (document no. CE-PT9L-12).

Perform USER INTERFACE design, implementation and FORMATIVE EVALUATION (5.8): The MANUFACTURER shall design and implement the USER INTERFACE, including the ACCOMPANYING DOCUMENTATION if needed, and training capability, if needed, as described in the USER INTERFACE SPECIFICATION. See section 6 and section 8 of Usability Engineering File (document no. CE-PT9L-12). The MANUFACTURER shall utilize, as appropriate, USABILITY ENGINEERING methods and techniques, including FORMATIVE EVALUATION to accomplish this design and implementation. The results of the utilized FORMATIVE EVALUATION shall be stored in the USABILITY ENGINEERING FILE. Where new USE ERRORS, HAZARDS, HAZARDOUS SITUATIONS or HAZARD-RELATED USE SCENARIOS are discovered during this step, the MANUFACTURER shall repeat the steps of Clause 5 as appropriate. Note: No new use error or hazardous situations were identified (status: N/A).
